question.problem:
Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with the following probability density function:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}5{x}^{4},\, & 0<x<1 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

If $Y=1-{X}^{5},$ then what is the probability density function of $Y?$
question.worked_solution:
To compute the probability density function of a random variable $Y,$ where $Y=u(X)$ is a continuous, strictly monotonic function of a continuous random variable $X,$ we follow two steps:

- First, we find an expression for ${F}_{Y}$ terms of ${F}_{X},$ where ${F}_{Y}$ and ${F}_{X}$ are the cumulative distribution functions of $Y$ and $X,$ respectively.

- Then, we differentiate ${F}_{Y}$ to get the probability density function ${f}_{Y}.$

Before we start, note that $Y=1-{X}^{5}$ is a strictly decreasing function of $X.$ Moreover, for $0<x<1,$ we have $0<y<1.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14231262/assets/05534475aecc1d0ebad2234f1259d1b6fd1c6183e47ad763f17c87c5fdb06afb.png)

Now, using the definition of the cumulative distribution of $Y,$ for $0<y<1,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}_{Y}(y) & =P(Y\le y) \\  & =P(1-{X}^{5}\le y) \\  & =P(-{X}^{5}\le y-1) \\  & =P(X\ge (1-y)^{1/5}) \\  & =1-{F}_{X}((1-y)^{1/5})\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the PDF ${f}_{Y}(y)$ for $0<y<1,$ we differentiate ${F}_{Y}$ with respect to $y$ using the chain rule. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={F}_{Y}^{′}(y) \\  & =0-(-\frac{1}{5(1-y)^{4/5}})\cdot {F}_{X}^{′}((1-y)^{1/5}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5(1-y)^{4/5}}\cdot {f}_{X}((1-y)^{1/5}).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the definition of ${f}_{X},$ we finally arrive at

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & =\frac{1}{5(1-y)^{4/5}}\cdot {f}_{X}((1-y)^{1/5}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5(1-y)^{4/5}}\cdot 5{((1-y)^{1/5})}^{4} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for the PDF of $Y$ is

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}1,\, & 0<y<1 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$
